identity.title: Position: Stop Automating Peer Review Without Rigorous Evaluation

problem.claim: Whether AI systems should be used to produce peer reviews amid the peer review crisis.

gap.claim: Automation requires a dedicated science of peer-review automation; general-purpose LLMs should not be deployed without rigorous evaluation.

contributions.claim: Argues that today's AI systems should not produce paper reviews.
Compares human- and AI-generated ICLR 2026 reviews and evaluates automated rewriting across different AI reviewers.
Identifies excessive reviewer agreement and stylistic gameability as critical problems for AI reviewing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AI reviewers show a cross- and within-paper “hivemind effect” of excessive agreement, reducing perspective diversity.

The authors report that prompting an LLM to rewrite a paper could significantly increase AI-reviewer scores, indicating susceptibility to stylistic paper laundering rather than changes in scientific results.
The authors report empirical comparisons involving ICLR 2026 reviews and automated rewriting across AI reviewers.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are presented as a tempting response to the peer review crisis.
The paper argues against using current AI systems to produce paper reviews.
The argument is grounded in human–AI review comparisons and tests of automated paper rewriting across AI reviewers.
The paper highlights reduced perspective diversity from agreement and score inflation from stylistic rewriting.
It frames non-gameability and review diversity as necessary but insufficient, calling for rigorous peer-review-automation science.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates necessary conditions from sufficient conditions: non-gameability and review diversity alone do not justify automation.

lessons.interpretation: This supports calibrating automation claims around explicit acceptance criteria rather than a single favorable metric.
lessons.application: Define multiple required criteria and state which additional criteria remain untested before recommending an automated reviewing system.
lessons.exception: Unsuitable when the work intentionally studies only one narrow property rather than making an overall deployment recommendation.

source_observation.claim: The evaluation includes adversarially relevant stylistic rewriting, exposing score changes without corresponding scientific-result changes.

lessons.interpretation: Robustness tests can reveal whether an evaluator tracks the intended object of assessment.
lessons.application: Add controlled presentation or rewriting perturbations when evaluating systems that score substantive quality.
lessons.exception: Less suitable when formatting or wording is itself the legitimate target of evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not report sample sizes, metrics, statistical details, or the magnitude of score increases.
It does not specify the additional conditions needed beyond diversity and non-gameability.
The abstract does not provide the evaluated models, rewriting prompts, or detailed comparison outcomes.
